visualReview.notes: The second set of renders shows the seven ascending gates, local flanks, separated temple, vaults, two-storey birthplace and stonework. Local plinths keep the buildings visible on the unsmoothed source terrain. Gate paving is shown in the detailed views where it follows the mapped route.

sharedSurfaceReview.notes: Inspected the darker basalt walls, dressed stone trim, timber and roof finishes, particularly the open Mahadarwaza portal and Amberkhana vaults. The shared flat stage isolates the meshes. The unchanged hillside is visible in the original-ground context.

mediumFiReview.notes: All four levels preserve the gate and summit layout. Wider terrain views show how small the built structures are relative to the hill. The close views show the open portals, vaults, two-storey birthplace and reservoir rim.

geographicReview.notes: Official visitor places and mapped trail access register the surviving structures to the original 1.8 km terrain crop with a 309 m elevation range. Gate orientations and local foundations are fitted estimates. No invented continuous wall rings across the natural cliffs and no terrain cuts.

fidelityReview.scope: The surviving public heritage ensemble at Shivneri: the seven stepped entrance gates and immediately connected stonework, Shivai Devi’s outer shrine, the Amberkhana vaults, summit memorial group and stone birthplace, Badami tank edge, Idgah and Kadelot. It is shown on the existing ridge. Rock-cut interiors and unidentified ruins are outside scope.
fidelityReview.notes: The public-domain Qualla photo sets the terrain context. Written records describe the seven openings and stone buildings. Gate profiles, local plinths, ornament, reservoir edging, and roof details are estimates. Rock-cut interiors and minor features were outside this model.

imageryReview.notes: The published Qualla landscape was traced to the exact creator-dedicated 2007 original. The documented crop and date-stamp removal outside the subject were compared to the original. No copyrighted or uncertain close imagery informed the model.

validation.sharedCaptureScope: The surviving Shivneri hilltop heritage group from the lower seven gates to the Shiv Janmasthan and Badami edging.

limitations: The seven masonry gates are located using visitor-stop coordinates and mapped paths. Orientations, immediate walls, heights and ornaments are approximate.
The modern birthplace mass is placed at the Archaeological Survey coordinate. Its unmapped footprint and roof construction are estimates.
The Badami reservoir has a visual edging only. Its water depth, rock-cut spring interiors and terrain drainage are outside the model. The original elevation grid is unchanged.
The open terrain cannot resolve every small terrace. The model uses estimated local retaining plinths where needed to keep standing structures above the original hillside.
The 2007 public-domain photograph is a distant landscape reference. Present close architectural details are interpreted from factual records and observed footprints.
